🚨🇺🇸🇮🇱 Nvidia’s regime change is a power play between money and the military, and the Israeli-linked faction just won the first round.

Simon Dixon joins Brandon to map the Jensen Huang affair scandal, the real chip flows to China, and why the next executives matter more than the founder.

Huang owned only 3–4% with no dual-class protection, so institutional holders (BlackRock, Vanguard, State Street) could move on him. Malaysia and Singapore have long bought far more Nvidia chips than they could use; everyone in the flows knew the end destination was China. 

The Alice Wong story (Singaporean tech executive, alleged Chinese influence ties are FBI unconfirmed) and the employee affair gave the board the governance hook it needed. Dixon says intelligence had the material earlier and released it after the midterms, as export-control fights peaked.

The incoming executives: at least two Israeli citizens, plus CFO Colette Kress who ran the Mellanox acquisition and whose first meetings were with the Israeli team. That side favors tighter controls and Taiwan escalation for war profits and cyber advantage; the financial side wants the revenue from China sales. 

Right now, the military/Israeli-aligned faction is ahead. China still holds the manufacturing and cost edge; the US keeps the IP. Data-center counts are misleading. China’s are state-scale; America’s are privatized and smaller. Taiwan’s silicon shield has roughly five years left, and its key staff is already choosing sides. 

Dixon is not hedging on the factions or the leverage.

@SimonDixonTwit @WeTheBrand

🚨🇺🇸 TRUMP’S THIRD-TERM WALL: 73% OPPOSE ANY RULE CHANGE AS THE GOP SPLITS

Pollster Mark Mitchell says the numbers were predictable months ago. 73% of Americans oppose changing the rules so Trump can run again. Only 27% support it. Even among Republicans, the figure is just 45%. Only 22% would back a constitutional amendment, and just 12% strongly.

MAGA never had a clear set of goals or core values beyond whatever Trump said it was. Now it is reduced to building ballrooms and bombing Iran. Mitchell warned in spring and summer 2025 that the right needed to start planning for what comes after MAGA. Almost nobody listened. The movement entered the midterms with the lowest presidential approval since Nixon, then watched independents deliver a roughly 15-point national swing against it.

The impeachment conversation is already real. A high-50s majority wants either immediate prioritization or at least a process. Trump’s response so far has been to dig in, dismiss the results, and keep talking about Iran. Among current Republicans, only about two-thirds flatly reject impeachment, and Republican party identification itself has already dropped several points.

Mitchell’s larger point is that the right cannot simply revert to Reagan-era conservatism. The base is anti-oligarchy and economically more progressive than party leaders admit, while still wanting border security and accountability. Neoconservative voices are already positioning for 2028, and JD Vance faces a choice: ride the current ship or create distance. The polling shows voters are done with the old formulas either way.

@WeTheBrandon @honestpollster
